newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia rebels say army violates accord.
newsitem.headline: Colombia rebels say army violates accord.

text.p: Tension mounted in a demilitarized zone of southern Colombia on Tuesday after leftist guerrillas, due to release 70 captive troops this weekend, complained of unauthorised army incursions.

The Defence Ministry issued a statement denying accusations that military helicopters flew over the 5,000 square mile (13,000 sq km) area of Caqueta province or that an army column had patrolled through part of the zone.
President Ernesto Samper repeated his pledge to court-martial any member of the armed forces found in the area in defiance of his order that the army pull out by June 23.

The jungle swathe was demilitarized to permit the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), the country's oldest and largest guerrilla army, to release 60 soldiers it captured more than nine months ago in neighbouring Putumayo province and 10 marines captured in a battle in northwest Choco province in January.

In a communique given to journalists in Cartagena del Chaira, the main town in the neutral zone, commanders of the FARC's so-called Southern Block warned the military manoeuvres could hamper the troop handover.

Defence Minister Gilberto Echeverri responded in a public statement: "The security forces of Colombia have strictly fulfilled the terms of the demilitarization ... planes can only fly over the area with the permission of ... the president and the defence ministry."

FARC guerrillas have been in complete control of the demilitarized zone for more than a week -- the first time the army ceded such a large area to the rebels. Last week the FARC said they would release their captives in Cartagena del Chaira on June 15.
The government's chief negotiator Jose Noe Rios on Tuesday played down suggestions that allegations of army incursions into the demilitarized zone could block the handover.
"Everything is on course for the troops to be handed over Sunday (June 15)," he told reporters.

The 60 soldiers were captured and 27 others were killed when FARC rebels overran the Las Delicias military base in an attack that marked one of the bloodiest guerrilla offensives in three decades of armed uprising in Colombia.
